newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Aggressive buying out of London swept South African bond yields lower and helped the rand two cents stronger in sporadic trade on Monday, dealers said.
The benchmark R150 stock was last quoted at a 15.84 percent yield from 16.00 percent on Friday and after trading as low as 15.805 percent late in the afternoon.
Dealers said that the main driving force behind the market's gains on the day was heavy buying out of London by a U.S. investment bank.
"(They) were very strong on the buying side...in tens and twentys (million rand)," a dealer said.
"And as the market went through critical levels at around 15.87 and 15.82, jobbers came in and covered their short positions," he added.
One trader put the offshore foray into the market at around 500 million rand.
"It was heavy trading from London," he said. "But it looked to be more of a blind punt than a well executed order...they were quite aggressive and could probably have bought at better levels."
Dealers said that after having moved down almost 20 basis points over the last two trading days, the market would probably take a breather on Tuesday and consolidate its gains.
They said that despite the day's move, the short-term mood remained bearish, particularly with the continuing cash crunch on the money market.
Short-term deposit rates remained static around the 17 percent level, despite an easing in the shortage to below the nine billion rand mark.

Three-month NCDs were quoted at between 16.95 percent offered and 17.20 percent bid, while the 90-day Bankers' Acceptance rate was in a 16.30 to 16.60 percent range compared with Friday's 16.30 to 16.75 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the shortage at 8.745 billion rand on Saturday from 8.8 billion rand on Friday.

Money market traders said they continued to expect the liquidity squeeze to last until Janury next year, as the Christmas spending period got into full gear, bringing more pressure to bear on banks' margins.
While the mood on the currency market was buoyed by the bond market's better performance, dealers said the rand's improvement came on the back of dollar selling out of London and the U.S.
"There are rumours of some big stop losses held by some U.S. funds below the 4.66 level...about $250 million," a trader said.
"We saw some dollar selling out of the U.S. and London attempting to trigger those stop losses so they could cover their short positions at a profit."
It ended at 4.6550/6600 against the dollar after touching a day's best of 4.6520 bid shortly before the official close and from 4.6780/6820 on Friday.
Volumes on the day had been thin, however, and dealers said further gains would depend on whether the rand made any further improvement from the 4.6550 level.
"If it can't get through the 4.65 level it will probably go back up to 4.67," the dealer said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.7711/7818 against sterling from 7.7966/8082 on Friday and at 0.3229/3234 marks from 0.3214/19 previously.
Foreigners sold a net 174.55 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 61.87 million rand worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 7.7 billion rand on Friday from 21.82 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
